title: Backend and Data Engineering
tagline: AI products are backend products. Services, databases, queues and pipelines.

topics.title: Building backend services
topics.summary: FastAPI-style services that front models and agents.
items: FastAPI / Starlette: routing, dependency injection, async, background tasks
Streaming responses (SSE, WebSockets) for token streaming
AuthN/AuthZ: OAuth2, OIDC, JWT, RBAC/ABAC, API key management
Multi-tenancy patterns
Rate limiting and quota systems (token bucket, sliding window)
Idempotency keys and request deduplication
Webhooks: signing, retries, ordering
Background jobs and queues: Celery, RQ, Arq, SQS, Kafka consumers
Long-running tasks: job IDs, polling, callbacks, resumability
Node/TypeScript backend basics (Next.js API routes, Hono, Express) for full-stack agents
gRPC services and protobuf contracts
questions: Design the API for a long-running agent task that the client can resume after disconnect.
Implement a per-user token-based rate limiter.

topics.title: Databases and storage
topics.summary: Pick the right store; know the internals.
items: Relational model, normalization, transactions, isolation levels, MVCC
Postgres in depth: indexes (B-tree, GIN, GiST, HNSW), EXPLAIN, vacuum, partitioning, JSONB
Connection pooling (PgBouncer) and why it matters for serverless
Replication, failover, read replicas, replication lag
NoSQL families: key-value (Redis, DynamoDB), document (MongoDB), wide-column (Cassandra), graph (Neo4j)
Redis: data structures, caching, pub/sub, streams, persistence trade-offs
LSM trees vs B-trees
Object storage (S3) semantics and consistency
Search engines: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch inverted index
OLAP: ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, DuckDB
Schema migrations and zero-downtime changes
Storing conversations, traces and agent state efficiently
questions: Explain isolation levels and a bug each one allows.
When would you not use Postgres?
Design the schema for storing agent conversation trees with branching.

topics.title: Queues, streams and events
items: Message queue vs log: SQS/RabbitMQ vs Kafka/Redpanda/Pulsar
Delivery semantics: at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once (and the truth about it)
Consumer groups, partitions, ordering guarantees
Dead-letter queues and poison messages
Outbox pattern, change data capture (Debezium)
Event sourcing and CQRS
Backpressure and load shedding
Sagas and compensating actions for multi-step workflows
questions: How do you get effectively-once processing?
Kafka vs SQS: how do you choose?

topics.title: Data pipelines and platforms
topics.summary: Training data, feature data, and analytics all need pipelines.
items: Batch vs streaming; lambda vs kappa architectures
Orchestrators: Airflow, Dagster, Prefect
Spark, Ray, Dask for distributed processing
dbt and analytics engineering
Lakehouse: Parquet, Delta, Iceberg, Hudi
Feature stores: Feast, Tecton; online vs offline consistency
Streaming: Flink, Spark Structured Streaming
Data contracts, lineage, catalogs, governance
Data quality testing and SLAs
questions: How do you prevent train/serve skew in features?
Design a pipeline that turns raw user conversations into a fine-tuning dataset safely.

items: React / Next.js fundamentals, server components, streaming
Streaming UI for tokens, tool calls and partial JSON
Generative UI and artifacts patterns
Vercel AI SDK, assistant-ui, CopilotKit
State management for long-running agent sessions
UX for trust: citations, progress, cancel, undo, approvals
Accessibility and latency perception
